newsitem.title: USA: CSCE cocoa ends higher in thin dealings.
newsitem.headline: CSCE cocoa ends higher in thin dealings.

text.p: CSCE cocoa futures ended moderately higher in dull activity Friday, buoyed by mixture of trade buying and light speculative shortcovering, floor sources said.

Most-active May delivery closed up $8 at $1,285 a tonne after ranging from $1,293 to $1,277. Spot March, which entered delivery period today, closed unchanged at $1,227, while the remaining months finished up $9 to $10.
Volume was light, at an estimated 5,617 lots, down sharply from Thursday's official tally of 18,304 lots.

Prices rose at the opening, encouraged by a slight easing of the dollar against sterling and a better-than-expected performance on the London market. But after briefly breaching near-term resistance at $1,291 in the May contract, buying interest subsided.
"It broke $1,291, but it did not follow through," one trader said. "It will probably have to get through $1,300 to get more speculators to cover shorts."
Traders expected CFTC's Commitments of Traders Report due late Friday to show an increase in speculative (non-commercial and nonreportable) short positions.
"If there are more spec shorts it may buoy the market," another dealer said. But he noted that despite today's gains, the May contract slid $16 on the week, and market direction is uncertain.
"No one really knows what this market is going to do," the trader said. "No one knows if it should correct or make new lows."
CSCE will be closed Monday in observance of Presidents Day.
